newsitem.title: CHINA: China can makers seen in price-cutting catastrophe.
newsitem.headline: China can makers seen in price-cutting catastrophe.

text.p: Over-production and price-cutting by China's ring-pull can makers will lead to catastrophe unless Beijing acts to cut costs, curb imports and stop new producers from entering the market, the China Daily said on Thursday.

Government action was needed to protect the ring-pull can industry, which could produce twice as many cans as China needed, the newspaper quoted Hu Zheng of the China Packaging Technology Association as saying.
Over-supply had forced producers to slash ring-pull can prices to just 0.95 yuan ($0.11) each by early 1996, down from 1.2 yuan a year earlier, Hu said.
"That will lead the industry to catastrophe in the long run," he said. "Some enterprises have been running with negligible profits or even in the red."
China's 21 ring-pull can makers had total capacity of more than 10 billion cans, to which new can plants under construction would add an estimated 3.0 billion more, the China Daily said.
However, demand in 1996 accounted for only 5.0 billion ring-pull cans, up from 4.0 billion in 1995, and was expected to be just over 8.0 billion by 2000, it quoted Hu as saying.
Experts believed existing enterprises should do more to cut production costs and to economise on raw materials while officials should be cautious about approving new can projects, the newspaper said.
Industry members were also calling on the government to crack down on illegal imports of ring-pull cans, it said but gave no details.
The quality of domestically-produced aluminium should be raised to replace imported raw materials, it said.

Almost half the 100,000 tonnes of aluminium used to make ring-pull cans in 1996 was smuggled into China from abroad, resulting in an estimated 130 million yuan in losses in potential tariff revenue, it said.
